verdict.reasoning: Patient says, "I've got a really bad headache, had it for about a day now." indicating a severe headache for one day.

Patient reports onset "ever since yesterday morning, since I woke up," "mainly on the left side," describes it as "kind of feels like it's throbbing, it's quite intense, sort of comes and goes," and adds "yeah, quite sensitive to light."

Patient states headache "seems to be worse, when I'm in a light room or like sunlight" and "think I've generally been lying down, seems to be better that way," supporting worsening in light and improvement lying down.

Doctor asks, "Is it worse when you lie flat, or when you bend forward?" Patient replies, "no," and when asked, "Any problems if you cough or sneeze?" patient answers, "Uh, no," supporting that these do not worsen the headache.

Patient denies visual problems ("any problems with your eyes, or your eyesight?" "Uh, no, not at all."), abnormal smells or tastes ("No."), nausea/vomiting ("no, no, been feeling fine"), URTI symptoms ("no, not really any sort of, cold symptoms"), fever ("I don't feel like I'm feverish, but I haven't checked."), skin changes ("No, skin feeling fine."), and neurological symptoms ("No, not at all" to weakness/tingling/numbness).

For intake: "have you been eating and drinking OK?" patient replies, "Yeah, yeah," and later confirms "Yeah, yeah, fine." Activity/rest: "What have you been doing since it came on?" Patient says, "mainly been at home."

Patient states, "no not really, it's not something I've, ever had before," and doctor summarizes, "this headache is new to you, and you've, you've not had regular headaches before?" Patient responds, "Yeah."
When asked about menstrual cycle, patient states, "no, not particularly, and my period was about a week ago," indicating last menses ~1 week ago and no clear relation.
In response to triggers, patient says, "may have been a bit stressed out at work, that kind of thing," indicating work stress.
When asked about significant medical problems, hospital admissions, operations, patient replies, "Uh, no, not recently, nothing," denying these issues.
When asked what tablets she has been taking, patient replies, "Uh, just Paracetamol," consistent with paracetamol as-needed use.
Patient states she takes "Microgynon, pill" and when asked when started: "about six years ago." On side effects: "not really, um, no, not too much."
Patient says, "I'm allergic to Aspirin, so I haven't been taking that." When asked what happens: "Um, I just feel really sick," indicating aspirin allergy manifested by nausea.
Patient reports, "my mum had, uh, high blood pressure, and she's got a history of migraines."
Living situation: "just with housemates, um, just friends." Alcohol: "probably, you know, a few drinks at the weekend." Smoking: "No." Other drugs: "No."

BP history: patient says she hasn't had it checked recently, then clarifies: "Yeah, yeah, so uh, probably about six months ago." and "It's always been fine I think," supporting approximately six months ago and normal.
Transcript documents an acute "really bad" left-sided, throbbing headache with photophobia for about a day, and doctor says, "it does, sound quite like a migraine," indicating likely migraine.

Doctor states, "What I would, suggest is, taking, uh, um, some anti-inflammatories, along with the Paracetamol," and later, "that would be the first thing to do, is to take some anti-inflammatories along with the Paracetamol. Make sure you're really well hydrated." Patient also repeats, "I'll take some Ibuprofen."

Doctor advises, "if it isn't settling, or it's getting worse, or you get any other change in your headache. Um, or you're unwell with it, with a high temperature, then we would certainly need to speak to you... If you have a raised temperature or, your headache's just getting worse, or you develop any rashes or anything like that. Then we'd need to speak to you straight away."

Doctor says, "if you're getting persistent, um, headaches, or headaches associated with your menstrual cycle, or certain things seem to trigger these headaches. Then, it, it would be worth, having a further discussion about it, to see whether we can, work out if we can help the, that longer-term," indicating follow-up for recurrent/triggered headaches (migraine management).
Doctor advises, "I would, try and arrange to get your blood pressure checked, if you haven't had it checked for a while."
Doctor states, "thing to do is to have a thermometer at home, so you can make sure that your temperature's OK," implying obtaining a home thermometer and monitoring temperature.
